newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China, Britain agree on HK's 1997-98 spending.
newsitem.headline: China, Britain agree on HK's 1997-98 spending.

text.p: China and Britain said on Thursday they reached agreement on Hong Kong's 1997-1998 budget spending and on cash to establish a post-colonial government after the colony reverts to China next year.
The British-ruled territory reverts to Beijing on July 1, 1997 as a Special Administrative Region of China .
The budget for the year to March 31 1998, which straddles the handover, has been under negotiation in a Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG) hammering out details of the flag change.
"In this round of talks, we have broadly speaking completed the resource allocation for the expenditure side of the budget," Britain's JLG representative Kwong Ki-chi told reporters.

"In the coming rounds, we'll be focusing on the revenue side. With the continued cooperation and mutual effort, we are confident we will achieve a 12-month budget for '97-'98," Kwong, Hong Kong's Treasury Secretary, said after a JLG meeting.
The transitional budget has been caught up in controversy with China criticising Hong Kong's policy on welfare spending, saying it was too generous.
